Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

hang around with verb

also hang out with, spend time with, go around with, keep company with

classical

Cic. Off. 2.13.46: quibuscum sī frequentēs sunt (Lewis & Short)
Liv. 39.53.11: fīlium frequentiōrem prope cum illīs quam sēcum cernēbat (Lewis & Short)

frequēns esse cum (+ abl.)

frequēns agrees with the subject

be often in someone’s company

Latin says it with an adjective: one is frequēns, “often present”, with someone.

Other words

  • frequēns adesse ūnā cum (+ abl.) — be often in someone’s company

    frequēns, “often present”, agreeing with the subject · also used · modern · Traupman 100; Traupman 325

    Traupman’s phrase. Every word is classical; we have found no classical instance of the phrase.

  • morārī cum (+ abl.) — spend time with, stay with

    also used · classical · Sen. Ep. 32.1: ubi et cum quibus morēris (Lewis & Short); Traupman 325

See also friend.
